magnitude.boundary: Population residing in countries classified at extremely high annual baseline water stress; not a count of households experiencing shortage.

threshold.classification: The 25-country group meets the source-defined extremely high category at more than 80 percent withdrawals relative to renewable supply.

momentum.boundary: Source-reported endpoint comparison; not a complete annual series and not used for historical percentiles.

source_snapshot.measurement_boundary: Aqueduct baseline water stress is modeled long-term demand divided by renewable supply. Population and agriculture figures are exposure estimates, not observed household shortages or basin depletion volumes.

transformations.formula: Normalize the source-reported global population share residing in countries at extremely high annual baseline water stress.
Map the WRI withdrawal-to-renewable-supply category boundaries, with 80 percent as the source-defined extreme threshold.
Normalize the conservative lower bound of a doubling in global demand since 1960 without inventing annual observations.
Use the source-reported share of global population exposed to high water stress for at least one month per year.

receipts.uncertainty: Aqueduct combines modeled renewable supply, sectoral withdrawals, population and spatial allocation. Country aggregation can hide basin variation; exposure is not realized shortage, and global demand more than doubled is an endpoint statement rather than a complete annual series.
receipts.freshness: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 global assessment 2023; snapshot refreshed 2026-07-31.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: WRI Aqueduct supplies a current global model, recognized 40% high and 80% extreme thresholds, annual extreme-stress exposure covering 25% of global population, a source-backed demand comparison since 1960, and monthly high-stress exposure covering 50% of global population.
